spec_questions: The two dia 5.5 dowel holes on the dia 30 circle reach r = 12.25, 0.75 mm inside the dia 26 boss. Cut through the flange only (Z 0..5), each leaves a 1.79 mm2 crescent roof under the boss, so they are not full through holes. Move them out to a circle of dia 32 or more, or accept a blind sliver.
The dia 4 set-screw hole at Z 22.6 reaches Z 24.6, leaving 0.4 mm to the boss top at Z 25: under the 0.6 mm minimum wall and under one hole diameter. Lower it to Z 20 or less, or lengthen the boss.
The set-screw hole is a plain dia 4 on one side (+Y) with no thread or tap-drill size (an M4 tap drill is 3.3).
No fillet or chamfer is given at the flange/boss junction, a stress raiser in a printed part, and no print direction is given (with the axis along Z the layers run across the boss).
B1.notes: Every cylinder centre and radius, the keyway planes and the set-screw axis were read back from the finished solid (REPORT.md). STL 0.25 % below the solid volume (faceting), inside the 0.5 % limit.

B2.print_orientation: layers stacked along Y (arm and plate lying flat on the bed, printed on their side)
B2.converged: von Mises yes (19.43, 19.33, 19.48 over three local sizes); tension across layers and interlayer shear no: they rise at the sharp side edges where the arm meets the plate (singular), so they are reported at the finest mesh
B2.verdict: PASS only in the Y-stacked orientation: factors 2.31 on yield, 2.5 on tension across layers and 2.4 on interlayer shear, all at the finest mesh. FAILS printed with layers along X (tension across layers 20.1 MPa, factor 1.12) or along Z (interlayer shear 7.3 MPa, factor 1.79). Thinnest margin 2.31; a 20 % higher load gives 1.93.
B2.notes: Support tried two ways: whole X0 face fixed (governing, 19.5) and the two screw-hole walls fixed (18.4 outside 3 mm of the holes; 26 at the hole mouth is the fixture singularity). Load as 60 N even pressure on a bonded 10 mm end block so the patch is its own face; the twin model has the same volume as the one-body part.

B4.how_tongue_was_stabilised: Four dia 1.8 x 3 mm soft pads (E 0.5 MPa) bonded to the tongue +-Y faces at x +-2, z 24, outer faces fixed; they carry 0.5 % of the load (sum of nodal reaction magnitudes 0.38 N of 80 N). The tongue is two bonded bodies split at Z 30 so the load patch is its own face. Two no-penetration contact sets (+X wall with +X face, -X wall with -X face). The floor was left out and shown not touched (15 to 20 micrometres of clearance left).
B4.valid: yes for forces, displacement and equilibrium; no for the block peak stress as a design number
B4.why: Reaction 80.0 N in X on three meshes (35.7k, 78.4k, 149.7k nodes). The shear force through the tongue is 80.0 N above the contacts (z 26 to 28) and 103.3 N between them, flat over z 10 to 18 and within 1.2 % across the meshes, which gives wall forces 183.3 and 103.3 N against the rigid-tongue hand 180.8 and 100.8 (1.4 % and 2.5 %). Contact is real: tongue and wall faces close to within 2 micrometres at the two contact lines and stay 0.1 to 0.28 mm apart elsewhere, and a reversed 0.001 N load moves the tongue 0.11 mm to the other wall. The block peak sits on the top edge of the +X wall, a sharp edge pressed by a flat face, and rises 35.0, 37.5, 41.0 MPa with refinement (singular); 3 mm below the edge the stress converges to 3.9 MPa and mid-wall to 2.5 MPa. A Hertz estimate with a 0.2 to 1 mm edge radius gives 57 to 127 MPa, so that edge will indent whatever the mesh says: chamfer or round it.
B4.notes: Integrating nodal stress over the wall faces gave 170 and 80 N (sum 90, 11 % off equilibrium) and was not used. About 11 minutes of the 40.
